doc.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: The 1924 Conn tenor and collecting horns
summary: He tells the story of buying a 1924 Conn tenor from an antique store and says he owns a couple of hundred instruments.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Tell me about this particular horn.

This is a Conn, made in 1924. I call it the flop ears because it’s got the bell keys on opposite sides, like Dumbo the Elephant. Got the flop ears in there, right? It’s a good old horn. It’s raggedy, it’s old, it’s worn out, it leaks.

It’s got some soul to it. I got it in an antique store for $77.50. It was in Maryland. I was a kid in school and I saw the horn there and I thought God, that’s the same as my grandfather’s alto, like a matching horn. Seventy-seven dollars? Gee. I went home and then I started agonizing about it. So I called up the store finally and said, “Do you still have that tenor saxophone?” They said, “Oh that was stolen.” I said, “Really? It was stolen?” And they said, “Yeah, we don’t have it. But they caught the guy who was stealing stuff.” And I said, “Really?” And they said, “Yeah, we might get it back.” So this started a long process. For months this went on and I kept calling them, and now I’m out of my mind — I should have bought that tenor, I should have bought that tenor. Finally they said, “Okay, we got the horn back, but we’re supposed to hold it as evidence. We’re not supposed to sell it until this whole case has been resolved.” And the thing dragged on and on. And finally I called them once again and they said, “All right, you know what? Come up here and get the horn.” So I drove up and bought the horn. Boy was I happy.
Boy. Every instrument you have seems to have a story behind it. © Hamilton Fillius Archive -12-

Yeah. Because I root around in antique shops and flea markets and I’m always, my hands are all dusty and dirty, going through piles of stuff, and you come across a lot of great things that way, and it’s a lot of fun.
How many instruments do you own?
Oh a couple of hundred probably.

Yeah, a lot, a lot. I have a whole big, it’s a sickness. Visit me if you’re in West New York/New Jersey, come over and visit me and you won’t believe what you see. I can’t believe it and I live there.
